When a future herdr build returns agent_prompt_stalled, re-run the gate scenario 5.

title: find_workspace: duplicate swarm labels shadow live workspaces
description:
## Background

The durable loop (and all flywheel commands) resolve a project to a herdr workspace by matching the label via `find_workspace` (main.rs:601) — it returns the FIRST workspace whose label equals `swarm_label(project)`. Two workspaces with the same label (e.g. a dead scratch swarm and a fresh spawn of the same project) make the command resolve to the STALE one: `flywheel status <project>` then reports 'no agents' even though the fresh swarm is idle and healthy.

Observed live during bd-send-stall-escalation e2e: the probe-drop left workspace w14 with label flywheel-scratch-e2e; a respawn created w15 with the same label. `flywheel status scratch-e2e` kept resolving to w14 (no agents) until w14 was closed manually. Same failure mode bites the loop itself: a resumed workflow poll can silently target the wrong workspace.

## Why

One stale workspace makes every flywheel command (status, loop, send, spawn) mis-resolve — silent wrong-target behavior in the orchestrator's core name resolution.

## Technical approach

- In `find_workspace` (main.rs:601-610): prefer the workspace that actually contains managed agents (`flywheel-<project>-` named agents); fall back to first-match only when none has agents. Or: warn + pick the newest workspace on ambiguity.
- Keep resolution deterministic (no clock-based nondeterminism in the durable path).
- Unit test the resolver (pure fn over a workspace list).
- e2e: spawn, kill agent (drop), respawn — status must resolve to the live workspace without manual closes.

## Success criteria

- Two same-label workspaces: `flywheel status` resolves to the one with live agents.
- No behavior change when only one workspace exists.
- Deterministic resolution (no reliance on wall-clock).
close_reason:
find_workspace now disambiguates duplicate swarm labels. Pure herdr::resolve_workspace_id(matches, agents, prefix): single match wins; duplicates -> prefer the workspace holding MANAGED agents (names starting with flywheel-<base>-); else the first match — deterministic, no wall clock in the durable path. find_workspace (main.rs) gathers the label matches, and only when >1 does it query the agent list (the single-match fast path stays one round trip) and call the resolver with the prefix built from project_base. 137/137 tests (5 new: single match, duplicate with live managed agent -> live, duplicates both dead -> first, duplicates both live -> first deterministically, nameless managed record does not count).

Live e2e (the exact bd-nil scenario): spawned scratch-e2e oc swarm, killed the agent (record dropped -> stale workspace w23, label flywheel-scratch-e2e, agent_status unknown), spawned a fresh pi swarm (w24, same label, agent idle). `flywheel status scratch-e2e` resolved to w24 (the live workspace with the named agent) — previously it resolved to w23 and reported "no agents". Workspaces cleaned up after.

title: pi agents spawn nameless: name-based resolution fails until manual rename
description:
## Background

`flywheel spawn --pi 1` calls herdr agent.start with a name (`flywheel-<project>-pi`), but the resulting agent record frequently has NO name field (herdr's pi integration does not register the name — unlike opencode agents which carry it). Name-based resolution then fails:

- `flywheel __send <project> <name>` -> 'agent not found'
- `--to pi` / resolve_agents matching by name -> no match
- the durable loop's `agent_target` falls back to the PANE ID, which breaks `read_output`/poll_kind lookups (the pane-id name does not resolve either)

Observed live during bd-send-stall-escalation e2e: the w18 pi agent came up nameless; the loop's CONTEXT_LIMIT guard then called poll_kind with the pane-id fallback name and crashed ('__kind failed: agent w18:p1 not found'). Renaming manually (`herdr agent rename <pane> <name>`) fixes it, and sometimes a fresh spawn registers the name correctly (w19 did) — the behavior is inconsistent.

## Why

The loop targets agents by name everywhere. A nameless agent makes the swarm unusable (send/status/loop all fail or misbehave).

## Technical approach

- Investigate herdr's agent.start/name persistence for pi (possibly a herdr-side timing/registration race).
- flywheel-side hardening: after spawn, verify the name landed (agent_list by pane) and re-apply `agent rename` until it sticks (bounded retries); or make `agent_target`/lookups fall back to pane id consistently (agent_target already does — the LOOKUP side needs the same fallback).
- e2e: spawn --pi, immediately status/send — must resolve without manual rename.
close_reason:
Spawn-time naming for nameless agent integrations. herdr.rs gains agent_rename (socket method agent.rename {target, name} — verified in the protocol schema). start_agent_with_retry (main.rs): after agent_start, the retry loop's name+pane match is extended — if a record exists on OUR pane with a missing/different name (the pi integration registers nameless), apply agent.rename(pane, requested-name) and return the named record. Name-based resolution (send/loop/status/--to) now works for pi swarms without manual `herdr agent rename`. 137/137 tests (incl. the resolver's nameless-record case).

Live e2e: `flywheel spawn scratch-e2e --pi 1` -> agent came up as flywheel-scratch-e2e-pi (named) with no manual intervention; status/send resolution worked immediately. (Previously w16/w18 pi agents came up nameless and required manual renames — see the 13b session notes.)

title: blocked status not producible via __send on this herdr build
description:
## Background

The e2e gate (bd-e2e-hardened-loop) scenario 4 drives an agent into herdr blocked (approval prompt) via __send prompts to verify the --on-blocked mail latency bound. On this build (herdr 0.7.5-preview), opencode agents auto-approve/execute ordinary prompts — none of the tested prompts (rm -rf /nonexistent, sudo -n true, etc.) produced an approval gate; the agent stayed working/idle.

## Why

The blocked-alert path (on-blocked mail within ~2x active interval) is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and wired (notify_blocked leaf), but never e2e-verified. A real blocked signal is the one herdr state this project cannot yet produce deterministically.

## Technical approach

- Try driving blocked via herdr agent send-keys into an opencode permission prompt, or a restricted-mode agent config (deny bash + request approval), or herdr's own blocked simulation if any (check herdr api schema for a state-forcing method).
- Alternatively verify the mail path end-to-end with a FAKE blocked: register the scratch project in agent-mail, then invoke __mail-blocked directly and assert delivery (the latency bound itself is already unit-covered).
close_reason: Discovery documented: herdr 0.7.5-preview cannot be driven into blocked via __send prompts (opencode auto-approves; rm/sudo prompts verified). The blocked-alert latency bound is unit-tested (next_interval_secs treats blocked as active) and the mail path is wired (notify_blocked leaf). The e2e gate (9qa) scenario 4 records this as its single FAIL with the precise reproduction; the gate script remains the runbook — when blocked becomes producible (or the __mail-blocked direct verification lands), scenario 4 flips green.

# flywheel integration generator — beads agent as per-tool subagents

## Background

The herdr-automation-hardening epic (closed 2026-08-04, all tracks) reworked the durable loop's
semantics: confirmed sends with landing, stall escalation with a 3-failure hard-stop, unknown
skip-dispatch + respawn, the state-file context contract, resume dedup via the last-sent registry,
and the adaptive cadence. After the epic, the beads-agent INSTRUCTIONS were stale in three places:
the v1 `## BEADS WORKFLOW` section duplicated across four identical AGENTS.md files
(~/.agents/AGENTS.md, ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md, ~/.grok/AGENTS.md, ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md), the
flywheel repo's own `br-agent-instructions-v1` block, and the daily-driver stage prompts (p4/p6).

## Architecture decision

The beads agent should be a generated **SUBAGENT per tool** (opencode/pi/grok) — NOT an AGENTS.md
section. Rationale: each tool has a first-class subagent mechanism (opencode `agents/`, grok
`agents/`, pi `agents/`); a subagent is loadable/invocable on demand, carries tool-specific
frontmatter (tools, thinking, permission modes), and the AGENTS.md stays a thin pointer. The
generator (`flywheel integration <kind>`) renders the subagent from templates so the installed
files stay current with the workflow after every flywheel rebuild.

## Why (justification)

"Update to newer changes" without a generator means hand-editing three or four files per workflow
change — the same duplication drift the v1 section suffered. A version-stamped generator makes the
integration a build artifact: edit `integrations/*.tpl`, rebuild, re-run, done.

## Bead set (children)

1. docs-research — per-tool instruction/command application points (discovery)
2. generator — `flywheel integration <kind> [--out]` CLI + templates (feature)
3. subagent-install — generate + install the beads subagent for opencode/pi/grok (feature)
4. shared-agentsmd-pointer — the 4 shared AGENTS.md copies: beads section -> subagent pointer
5. repo-agentsmd-v2 — flywheel repo AGENTS.md: br-agent-instructions v1 -> v2
6. stage-prompts — STAGES p4/p6 revised to the full lifecycle
7. docs-skill — README section + flywheel skill 0.2.1 + CHANGELOG entries

All children are IMPLEMENTED and CLOSED with evidence (the work landed in commit d853ebd on the
flywheel repo + skill 0.2.1 on ~/.agents); the beads exist to document the design and the
regeneration flow for the future self.

## Over-arching goal

flywheel must be the hands-off swarm orchestrator: spawn a swarm, walk away, come back to complete
work. The beads subagent is the per-agent brain that makes the swarm's execution uniform and
correct; the generator keeps that brain in sync with the orchestrator's semantics forever.

# Per-tool instruction/command application points (docs research)

## Background

To place the beads agent correctly for opencode/pi/grok, the authoritative docs of each tool were
consulted to learn WHERE agent instructions, subagents, and commands are applied. This bead
captures the findings — the "map" that every other bead in the epic depends on.

## Findings (verified against each tool's docs/config)

### Grok (~/.grok, bundled README.md ~107KB)
- **Agent rules**: `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` = GLOBAL rules (scanned FIRST), then every repo-root→cwd
  directory, then only cwd outside git repos. Filenames checked per dir: Agents.md, Claude.md,
  AGENT.md, AGENTS.md. Deeper files take precedence. 10,000-char cap per file (truncated with a
  warning). `--rules` flag appends additional rules.
- **Subagents**: `~/.grok/agents/<name>.md` — frontmatter: name, description, prompt_mode,
  model, permission_mode, agents_md.
- **Commands/skills**: `~/.grok/skills/` (beads-*, swarm, br, bv, agent-mail already installed),
  `~/.grok/hooks/`, `~/.grok/config.toml`.

### Opencode (~/.config/opencode)
- **Agent rules**: `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` = global instructions (read alongside cwd
  AGENTS.md).
- **Subagents**: `~/.config/opencode/agents/<name>.md` — frontmatter: name, description, mode
  (primary/subagent), temperature, tools allowlist (e.g. mcp-agent-mail_*, read/write/edit/bash/
  grep/glob/task). Managed via `opencode agent create|list`.
- **Commands**: `~/.config/opencode/command/<name>.md` — slash commands with frontmatter
  (description, agent: beads); beads-create/execute/review/commit + swarm already exist and wrap
  the daily-driver stages with the lifecycle.
- The bundled ~/.config/opencode/README.md is the OpenAgents framework README (not opencode's own
  docs) — do not consult it for opencode semantics.

### Pi (~/.pi)
- **Agent rules**: `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (the agent dir holds it; identical to the other two
  copies).
- **Subagents**: `~/.pi/agent/agents/<name>.md` — frontmatter: name, description, aliases,
  thinking, systemPromptMode (replace), inheritProjectContext, inheritSkills, tools (read, grep,
  find, ls, bash, edit, write, mcp:agent-mail, contact_supervisor), defaultContext, defaultReads,

  frontmatter is the source.
- **Commands/extensions**: `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (herdr-agent-state.ts is herdr-managed —
  never edit), `pi --append-system-prompt`, `pi config`.

## Reasoning

The subagent dirs all exist and already contain a v1 `beads.md` — the architecture target is to
REGENERATE those files from templates, not invent new mechanisms. Config dirs confirmed:
~/.config/opencode, ~/.pi, ~/.grok.

- The three subagent dirs + their existing beads.md files identified (opencode/pi/grok).
- The AGENTS.md global-rule mechanism confirmed for all three.
- The v1-era bodies assessed (grok/pi = 47-line v1; opencode = fuller but missing the context
  contract).

## Status

IMPLEMENTED — research done during the integration work (2026-08-04); documented here for the
future self. No code changes.

# Changelog automation via git-cliff + semantic versioning

## Background

The flywheel repo had no CHANGELOG.md, no tags, and a mixed commit history
(conventional commits like `feat(herdr):` mixed with bead-prefixed ones like
`bd-send-stall-escalation-13b: ...`). Releases were unmanaged: the crate sat
at 0.1.0 through the entire hardening epic. This bead sets up generated
changelogs + semver so "what changed since last release" is one command.

## Technical approach (implemented)

- **cliff.toml** (git-cliff 2.13, installed via brew): Keep a Changelog header
  + semantic versioning notice; `conventional_commits = true` with
  `filter_unconventional = false` (the history mixes styles — keep both);
  `commit_preprocessors` strips the `bd-<id>: ` prefix (hyphen-tolerant regex)
  and collapses `beads:`/`close epic:` prefixes; `commit_parsers` group:
  conventional types (feat/fix/docs/perf/refactor/style/test/chore) + the
  bead-landing subjects (escalate/respawn/state-file/adaptive/interval/
  registry/wait-output/context-verdict/confirm/dedupe/integration-gate ->
  Features; duplicate-label/pi-nameless -> Bug Fixes; clippy -> Misc); the
  body template renders subject-only lines (`split(pat="\n") | first`) so
  multi-line commit bodies never leak in.
- **CHANGELOG.md** generated: 29 entries — 16 Features (the hardening epic
  tracks + the integration generator), 3 Bug Fixes, 1 Documentation, 2
  Miscellaneous (protocol v18 docs bump, clippy zero-warnings), 4 Other
  (epic creation/close, ojx evidence, backtick-restore).
- **Version 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0** in Cargo.toml (semantic: the epic added
  features; no breaking CLI changes). The binary's `--version` follows.
- **README** "Changelog / releases" section: regenerate
  (`git cliff -o CHANGELOG.md`), preview (`git cliff --unreleased`), release
  (`git cliff --bump` bumps version + tags vX.Y.Z + writes the changelog).

## Reasoning

git-cliff (Rust, standalone) fits the Rust repo better than the Node
(standard-version/semantic-release) or Python (commitizen) alternatives; the
bead-prefix preprocessors make the ENTIRE history automatable instead of
filtering out the epic's commits. Generated-only changelogs (no hand edits)
keep the file reproducible.

## Success criteria (verified)

- `git cliff -o CHANGELOG.md` regenerates cleanly and idempotently.
- All history lands in sensible groups (no stray multi-line bodies).
- `flywheel --version` reports 0.2.0 after the rebuild + reinstall.

## Test plan

- Manual: regenerate + diff against the committed CHANGELOG.md (idempotent).
- Future: after each release, `git cliff --bump` produces the versioned
  section + tag; the [Unreleased] section accumulates the next cycle.

## Considerations

- Tags did not exist at setup time — the initial changelog is one
  [Unreleased] block; the first `git cliff --bump` anchors v0.2.0.
- git-cliff 2.13 has no `--dry-run` (removed) — preview via `--unreleased`.
- Commit conventions going forward: conventional commits preferred; the
  bead-prefixed style remains supported by the parsers.
close_reason: Implemented + verified (commit ed4655a): cliff.toml with Keep-a-Changelog output + conventional + bead-prefixed parsers (preprocessors strip bd-<id>: prefixes, subject-only template); CHANGELOG.md generated with 29 entries grouped correctly; Cargo.toml bumped 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0; flywheel --version reports 0.2.0; README documents the regenerate/preview/release flow (git cliff --bump for releases). Regeneration verified idempotent. 140/140 tests, clippy clean.

title: Event-driven agent collaboration spine (epic)
description:
# Event-driven agent collaboration spine — umbrella epic

## Background

flywheel is a herdr-backed swarm orchestrator with a Resonate-durable monitoring loop. A 2026-08-05 audit (ADR-0001) measured six defects against the live herdr 0.8.0-preview (protocol 19) and the running agent-mail MCP (46 tools):

- **A1** protocol pin stale (18 vs live 19) — `src/herdr.rs:19`
- **A2** the loop polls; `events.subscribe` (already implemented at `src/herdr.rs:311`) is unused; SSE is faked from the poll stream (README:195)
- **A3** only 8 of 46 agent-mail tools are wrapped in `src/mail.rs`; `register_agent`/`reply_message`/`acknowledge_message`/`renew_file_reservations`/`acquire_build_slot`/`search_messages`/`request_contact`/macros all unused
- **A4** herdr pane IDs (`wT:p1`) are never bridged into agent-mail identities → `resolve_pane_identity` returns nothing for herdr panes → peers unaddressable
- **A5** `unknown`/`exited` agent states are observed but never recovered (`src/durable.rs:549`) — black hole
- **A6** `--on-blocked mail` fires once and returns (`src/durable.rs:512`) — no escalation

These six together mean flywheel is a **poll-based, orchestrator-only, one-directional** swarm. The captain's question — *can agents signal/trigger each other autonomously, without HITL, for debate loops / plan-review-implement / peer handoffs / cross-project swarms?* — is answerable **no** today, not because the primitives are missing from the dependencies, but because flywheel doesn't use them.

## Goal of this epic

Upgrade flywheel to an **event-driven, peer-capable, bidirectionally-coordinating collaboration spine**. Six phases (each a child task group below): protocol/schema currency → event-driven loop → mail surface expansion → blocked escalation → collaboration recipes → tests/docs.

## Why it matters (overarching project goal)

This is the foundational coordination architecture for everything the project aspires to: multi-agent debates, autonomous plan-review gates, self-healing swarms, cross-project fan-out (hachiko ↔ flywheel ↔ toron). Without it those patterns are unreachable. Reliability fixes (A1/A5/A6) must land before or alongside the collaboration primitives (A2/A3/A4) — coordinating fast into a silently-dying swarm is worse than polling.

## Out of scope

- Changing the Resonate `swarm_loop` workflow topology (events feed *leaves*, not the workflow — see ADR-0001 §5).
- Migrating to a different coordination backend (NATS/Redis). Rejected in ADR-0001 §5.
- Auto-accepting all contact requests globally (`policy=open`). Default stays `auto`.

## Child phases

- Phase 1 — Protocol & schema currency (3 beads)
- Phase 2 — Event-driven loop core (3 beads)
- Phase 3 — agent-mail surface expansion (8 beads)
- Phase 4 — Blocked escalation protocol (1 bead)
- Phase 5 — Collaboration pattern recipes (4 beads)
- Phase 6 — Tests & hardening (3 beads)

## Success Criteria

1. `flywheel loop` dispatches in event-time (<500ms after a peer hits `done`), not poll-time (~30s).
2. Every spawned agent is a registered, resolvable agent-mail identity.
3. All four collaboration patterns (§9 of ADR-0001) have a documented recipe + passing e2e test.
4. `unknown`/`exited` states self-heal within a bounded retry budget.
5. `docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0001.sh` passes.

## Reference

- ADR: `docs/decisions/0001-event-driven-agent-collaboration-spine.md` (full evidence, alternatives, consequences).
- Prior epic (historical, status=open in base.jsonl): `bd-herdr-automation-hardening-q9t` + 17 children. This epic is the next phase.

# protocol-v19-bump — bump herdr socket protocol pin 18 → 19

## Background

`src/herdr.rs:19` pins `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18;`. The live herdr binary reports `"protocol": 19` (0.8.0-preview.2026-08-04-d78e3d3b5126, verified via `herdr api schema --json`). The `bd-deps-protocol-check` bead (prior epic) made `flywheel deps` *warn* on mismatch — but the **pin itself is stale**, so the check is self-defeating: it warns about a drift the project never caught up to. Protocol 19 added fields flywheel's wire structs already tolerate via `#[allow(dead_code)]` (`agent_session`, `interactive_ready`, `state_labels`, `foreground_cwd`), but the next protocol bump that adds a *required* request field will break the client at runtime with no compile-time signal. This is ADR-0001 gap A1.

This bead is **foundational and blocking**: confident event typing (Phase 2) and any new request payloads depend on knowing we speak the live protocol.

## Subtasks

1. Run `herdr api schema --output /tmp/herdr_schema.json` and diff the wire structs in `src/herdr.rs` (`AgentInfo`, `WorkspaceInfo`, `PaneInfo`, `WorktreeInfo`, `AgentSessionInfo`, `PaneAgentStatusChanged`) against the schema's `$defs`. Promote any field the schema now marks `required` from `#[serde(default)]` / `Option<T>` where the contract changed; add any new typed struct for fields currently swallowed as `serde_json::Value`.
2. Bump `HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18` → `19`.
3. Update the module doc comment (`src/herdr.rs:9-12`) — "Verified against herdr 0.7.5-preview (socket protocol v18...)" → 0.8.0-preview protocol v19, build hash `d78e3d3b5126`.
4. Update `AGENTS.md` "herdr protocol v18" → v19, and `README.md:168` "socket protocol v18" → v19.

## Approach notes

- Do NOT change request payloads in this bead — only the pin + struct currency + docs. Forward-compat of the *check* itself is the next bead (`bd-protocol-forward-range`).
- Keep `#[allow(dead_code)]` on fields flywheel doesn't consume yet — they must still deserialize. The contract is "parse everything the server sends"; the client opts into consuming fields incrementally.
- If the schema diff reveals a *removed* field or renamed enum variant that flywheel reads, that's a real breaking change — stop and add a subtask for it; do not paper over it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HDR_PROTOCOL == 19`.
- `flywheel deps` against the live herdr binary reports no protocol warning.
- All existing `herdr.rs` unit tests pass; `cargo build --release` clean.

## Test plan

- Unit: extend the existing protocol-parse test to assert `parse_protocol` reads 19 from a real schema JSON fixture (commit a trimmed fixture under `src/` or `tests/fixtures/`).
- Manual: `flywheel deps` shows green; `herdr api snapshot` round-trips through `Client::agents()` without serde errors.

## Considerations

- The pin is a *single source of truth* (`bd-deps-protocol-check`'s whole point). Bumping it must be deliberate, not a silent drift fix — hence this bead, not a drive-by.
- Forward-range comes next; here we just catch up.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A1), §7 Phase 1, §11 verification (a).
close_reason: HDR_PROTOCOL 18->19; wire structs promoted to live schema contract (AgentInfo.agent_status non-Option, WorkspaceInfo +number/focused/active_tab_id, PaneInfo +terminal_id/focused, WorktreeInfo workspace_id->open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools, AgentSessionInfo/PaneAgentStatusChanged already conformant); module doc + AGENTS.md + README updated to 0.8.0-preview d78e3d3b5126; trimmed live schema fixture committed (tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) with parse_protocol fixture test; 160 tests pass incl live snapshot round-trip (worktree.list now parses live wire); clippy clean; release build clean; flywheel deps shows 'herdr protocol: 19 (expected 19)' no warning

title: protocol-forward-range: deps check == -> >= forward-compat
description:
# protocol-forward-range — flip the deps protocol check from `==` to `>=`

## Background

The `bd-deps-protocol-check` bead shipped a `flywheel deps` warning when the live herdr `protocol` field ≠ `HDR_PROTOCOL`. That's an **equality** check: every herdr release that bumps the protocol (even additively) forces a flywheel release, or every `flywheel deps` run screams. The pin-then-bump cycle (`bd-protocol-v19-bump`) is brittle — it treats forward-compatible protocol additions as breakage. This is the structural fix under ADR-0001 gap A1.

herdr's protocol is *additive by design*: new optional fields, new event variants, new optional request params. A higher live protocol number than the pin is **safe** (the client ignores what it doesn't know); a *lower* one is unsafe (server may not understand our requests). The check should encode that asymmetry.

## Subtasks

1. Find the comparison site (search `src/` for `HDR_PROTOCOL` usage in the `deps` command handler; likely `src/main.rs` `cmd_deps` or a helper). It currently compares `live == HDR_PROTOCOL`.
2. Change the semantics: `live >= HDR_PROTOCOL` = OK (forward-compat); `live < HDR_PROTOCOL` = ERROR (server too old, our requests may be rejected); equality mismatch where `live > HDR_PROTOCOL` = INFO/WARN ("server newer than verified; client may not use new features, but safe").
3. Update the warning text to distinguish the three states with actionable copy (e.g. "server protocol 19 < pinned 20: downgrade herdr or rebuild flywheel against newer schema").
4. Add a regression test exercising all three branches with synthetic schema JSON.

## Approach notes

- The "server newer" INFO path is important: it tells a future maintainer "we haven't caught up to this protocol yet" without alarming a user. That's the signal that triggers a `bd-protocol-v2X-bump` bead later.
- Keep `HDR_PROTOCOL` as the *verified* floor, not the ceiling. Document this in the module doc comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 19 and pin 19 → green.
- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 20 and pin 19 → INFO (not error).
- `flywheel deps` with live protocol 18 and pin 19 → ERROR with actionable message.
- All three covered by unit tests.

## Test plan

- Unit: table-driven test over `(live, pin) -> Severity` triples in the deps handler module.

## Considerations

- This change is small but load-bearing: it determines whether every future herdr upgrade is a 5-minute docs update or a forced flywheel release. Get the semantics right once.
- Do not weaken the `< pin` case — that's the real safety net.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A1), §4 commitment 1, §5 (rejected: keep equality), §11 (a).
close_reason: Flipped deps protocol check == to >= semantics (ADR-0001 A1). ProtocolCheck enum {Match,Newer,Older} + pure protocol_check(live,pin) in main.rs; HDR_PROTOCOL now the verified FLOOR: live==pin green, live>pin INFO (forward-compat, additive-by-design; signal for future bump bead), live<pin ERROR + exit 1 (ok=false -> bail, verified at cmd_deps tail). Actionable copy per branch. Stale 'protocol v18' capabilities string now derives from HDR_PROTOCOL (v19). Verified live: flywheel deps -> 'herdr protocol: 19 (verified 19)' exit 0; capabilities -> v19. Table-driven test: 7 (live,pin) triples. 177 tests pass, clippy clean, release deployed.

title: schema-event-typing: type all 26 herdr event variants
description:
# schema-event-typing — type all 26 herdr event variants + subscription events

## Background

`src/herdr.rs` defines `PushEvent { kind: String, data: Value }` and a handful of typed event structs (`PaneAgentStatusChanged`). The live schema (`herdr api schema --json`) enumerates **26 event types** (workspace_*, worktree_*, tab_*, pane_*, layout_updated) and **subscription events** (`PaneAgentStatusChangedEvent`, `PaneOutputMatchedEvent`, `PaneScrollChangedEvent`). Today every event's `data` is an untyped `serde_json::Value` — the loop must match on `kind` strings and hand-parse `Value` at every call site. That's fragile and blocks the Phase-2 event reactor, which needs to destructure events deterministically. This is the typing foundation for ADR-0001 gap A2.

Depends on `bd-protocol-v19-bump` (struct currency first).

## Subtasks

1. Generate/author typed Rust structs for each of the 26 event payloads, grouped by domain (`WorkspaceEvent`, `TabEvent`, `PaneEvent`, `WorktreeEvent`, `LayoutEvent`) or one enum `HerdrEvent` with 26 variants — pick the shape that deserializes cleanly via `#[serde(tag = "type", content = "...")]`. The schema's `EventData.oneOf` (tagged by `type` const) is the template.
2. Add the three subscription-event structs (`PaneOutputMatchedEvent` with match text + pane id; `PaneScrollChangedEvent` with scroll info).
3. Replace `PushEvent { kind: String, data: Value }` with `PushEvent { event: HerdrEvent }` (or keep `kind` as a convenience accessor). Keep back-compat for any existing `kind`-string matchers, or migrate them.
4. Add an `EventFilter`/`Subscription` builder that types the subscription request (currently `Subscription` is stringly-typed at `src/herdr.rs` ~line 290-310).
5. Serde round-trip tests for every variant using fixtures carved from a real `events.subscribe` capture (or hand-built from the schema).

## Approach notes

- Use `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` + tagged enums to match herdr's `{"type": "pane_agent_status_changed", ...}` wire shape exactly. Verify against a live capture, not just the schema JSON (schema is the contract; capture is reality).
- Don't over-model: fields flywheel doesn't consume yet stay `#[serde(default)] #[allow(dead_code)]`. The goal is *type safety for the fields we route on* (`agent_status`, `pane_id`, `agent`, `workspace_id`, `type`).
- The `PaneAgentStatusChanged` struct already exists — extend the pattern, don't reinvent it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EventStream::read_event` returns a typed `HerdrEvent`, not `(String, Value)`.
- All 26 variants + 3 subscription events deserialize from fixtures without error.
- `br`/`cargo test` green; clippy clean.

## Test plan

- Unit: one round-trip test per variant (26 + 3). Fixtures in `tests/fixtures/herdr-events/*.json`.
- Property-style: a captured multi-event stream parses end-to-end into a `Vec<HerdrEvent>` with no `Value` leakage in the consumed fields.

## Considerations

- Tagged-enum serde can be finicky with `content` field naming per variant — the schema uses different content keys (`workspace` vs `workspace_id` vs `pane` vs `panes`). An externally-tagged `#[serde(tag="type")]` flat enum may not fit; a manually-implemented `Deserialize` that reads `type` then dispatches is more robust. Budget for that.
- This bead is pure typing — no behavior change. Keeps the Phase-2 reactor bead small and reviewable.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2), §7 Phase 1, §11 (c).
- Schema: `/tmp/herdr_schema.json` (regenerate with `herdr api schema --output`).
close_reason: Typed all 29 herdr event variants (26 server snake + 3 subscription dotted). PushEvent{kind: HerdrEventKind, data: HerdrEventData} with manual Deserialize dispatching on the envelope 'event' field; payload structs per live schema oneOf (reused PaneInfo/WorktreeInfo; minimal WorkspaceInfo/TabInfo/PaneScrollInfo; Layout/read stay Value — unconsumed). Subscription builder now encodes the REAL v19 contract: pane.agent_status_changed REQUIRES pane_id (verified live — null pane_id was silently rejecting every watch subscription since v19 bump, poll-fallback masked it). cmd_watch subscribes per-pane; poll fallback extracted (watch_poll). 29 schema-derived fixtures parse (all_event_fixtures_parse_typed + parse_push_event updated); kind_wire_roundtrip (29) + subscription_to_value_wire_shape tests. LIVE PROOF: self-driving ignored test (free pane -> subscribe -> agent.start -> agent.prompt -> typed pushes parsed, 0 Value leakage) + raw capture pane.agent_status_changed push. 180 tests, clippy -D warnings clean, release deployed.

title: event-subscribe-reactor: events.subscribe as loop primary signal
description:
# event-subscribe-reactor — `events.subscribe` as the loop's primary signal (Resonate-correct, forward-only-honest)

> **Polish revision (round 2):** schema-verified correction. `herdr api schema` confirms
> `events.subscribe` takes ONLY event-type filters (`EventsSubscribeParams.subscriptions`),
> with **no `since`/`after_seq`/cursor parameter — the stream is forward-only; no replay.**
> Round 1's wording ("re-reads the still-open subscription from the cursor — no event loss")
> overpromised a replay capability herdr doesn't have. **Corrected design:** the event stream
> is a **latency optimization** (sub-500ms dispatch while running); the **heartbeat `__poll` is
> the correctness floor** (full-state reconciliation catches any change missed during a crash/
> restart gap, because `agent.list` is an authoritative current-state snapshot, not event
> history). The cursor is demoted to optional best-effort intra-run dedup — NOT a replay
> guarantee. This is simpler and honest.
>
> **Round 1 redesign stands:** event-polling is a **Resonate leaf `__poll_events`** (not an
> in-workflow tokio channel — that broke replay determinism). Cursor or not, the leaf pattern
> honors AGENTS.md ("leaves take simple identifier params, return the prelude Result").

## Background

The durable loop (`swarm_loop` at `src/durable.rs:853`, `async fn swarm_loop(ctx: &Context, params: LoopParams)`) samples swarm state every `interval_secs` (default 30s) via `ctx.run(__poll)` + `ctx.sleep`. herdr exposes a real push event stream (26 types; `EventStream::subscribe` at `src/herdr.rs:311-380`, **called nowhere in the loop**). This is ADR-0001 gap A2 — the biggest collaboration-latency bug (up to 30s to detect a peer hitting `done`; transient states collapse to one sample).

Depends on `schema-event-typing` (typed events) + `loop-state-schema-v2` (escalation/respawn state — the cursor field there is now optional per this revision).

## Subtasks

1. Add a hidden leaf `__poll_events` (sibling to `__poll`/`__send`) — a plain binary subprocess (NOT a Resonate generator) that:
   - opens a fresh `EventStream` subscription on the project workspace, filtered to `pane.agent_status_changed` + `pane.agent_detected` + `pane_exited` (NOT `pane.output_changed` — high volume),
   - **blocks with a bounded timeout** (`heartbeat_interval`, default = the old `interval_secs` or 2× it),
   - prints the JSON batch of events that arrived within the timeout `[{event}, ...]`, exit 0. **Forward-only** — herdr delivers from subscribe-time forward; there is no replay (verified: `EventsSubscribeParams` has no since/seq param).
2. Rewrite the `swarm_loop` dispatch driver: each iteration, `ctx.run(__poll_events, timeout=heartbeat_interval)`:
   - **fast path:** if events arrived → update cached state, route them (`bd-event-dispatch-zero-latency`), continue (sub-500ms dispatch).
   - **correctness path:** every Nth iteration (default N=1 — i.e. reconcile every heartbeat regardless) AND on `__poll_events` error/timeout-with-zero-events, run `ctx.run(__poll)` to **reconcile full state** from the authoritative `agent.list` snapshot. This is the floor that catches any state change missed during a crash/restart gap (events are not replayed; the snapshot IS the truth).
   - then `ctx.sleep(next_deadline)` where `next_deadline` is short when events are flowing, the full heartbeat when idle.
3. **Crash-resume correctness (the honest contract):** on resume, the first iteration's `__poll` (correctness path) reconciles full current state — any event whose effect was missed during the offline gap is captured by the snapshot. **No event replay is attempted or claimed.** The loop may redispatch an agent that finished during the gap one heartbeat later than ideal — acceptable; the heartbeat bounds it.
4. **Cursor (optional, best-effort, demoted):** track `max(state_change_seq)` seen in `loops.json` (`bd-loop-state-schema-v2` field). Use it ONLY to skip events on the live stream with `seq <= cursor` that the loop already processed this run (defensive dedup against any same-connection re-delivery). **Do NOT rely on it for crash recovery** — the heartbeat snapshot is the recovery mechanism. If the cursor adds complexity without measurable dedup benefit in testing, drop it (the cached-state dedup may suffice).
5. Structured logging: every routed event logs `{ts, event_type, pane_id, agent, prev_status, new_status, action}` to the event log (`state.rs::log_event`) — the audit trail + the parity-test's evidence source.
6. Health: if `__poll_events` errors 3× consecutively, force `__poll` + log "event stream may be dead; heartbeat fallback active" at WARN (the loop keeps running correctly, just at heartbeat latency).

## Approach notes

- **The leaf is the key to Resonate-correctness.** `__poll_events` is a subprocess doing blocking socket I/O, returning a deterministic batch; the workflow calls it via `ctx.run`, which replays on crash. No in-workflow channel, no non-determinism (same pattern as `__poll`/`__send` — just event-shaped).
- **Forward-only is fine because the heartbeat is authoritative.** herdr's `agent.list` returns current pane/agent state (status, cwd, agent_session) — a full snapshot. Reconciling against it every heartbeat means the loop's cached state converges to truth regardless of missed events. The event stream's ONLY job is to make dispatch faster *while running* (the collaboration-latency win for debate/peer-triggered patterns).
- **Don't over-engineer the cursor.** It was load-bearing in round 1 (replay) — demoted to optional dedup in round 2 (forward-only reality). If testing shows cached-state dedup suffices, remove the field entirely. Prefer the simpler design.
- Resonate constraint (AGENTS.md): leaves take **simple identifier params** — pass `project` + optional `cursor_json` (a string), not a tuple. Return the prelude `Result`. `ctx.run`/`ctx.sleep` are the only awaits in the workflow.
- Subscribe per-workspace-id (resolved at loop start), not global — a 5-workspace host shouldn't fan every pane event into every loop.
- `swarm_loop` is at `durable.rs:853` and already uses `ctx.run` (lines 822/832/1080/1092) + `ctx.sleep` (1142) — this bead adds one more `ctx.run` leaf (`__poll_events`) to that existing structure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A peer hitting `done` while the loop is running is redispatched in <500ms p95 (measured) — the latency win.
- Killing the event stream mid-loop does not stall or corrupt state — heartbeat `__poll` reconciliation takes over; cached state converges to truth within one heartbeat.
- **Crash-resume correctness:** after a kill/restart, the first heartbeat `__poll` reconciles full state; no agent is permanently stuck or double-dispatched (verified by the durability test). The loop makes NO claim of event replay.
- Event log captures every routed event with the structured fields above.
- `br lint` clean; `cargo test` green.

## Test plan

- Unit: state-update/route table-driven over event × cached-state.
- Integration (isolated herdr session `test-parity`): scripted agents flip `working`→`done`; assert dispatch latency < 500ms p95 + event-log entries present.
- **Durability (the honest contract):** kill loop mid-run; restart; assert (a) no agent double-dispatched, (b) no agent permanently stuck (heartbeat reconciles), (c) an agent that finished during the gap is redispatched within one heartbeat of resume. Do NOT assert zero event loss (forward-only stream makes that impossible; the snapshot reconciles).
- Parity: `bd-test-event-poll-parity` (event path == poll path *final state*, not *event sequence*).
- Degradation: kill event stream; assert heartbeat fallback + WARN log within `2 × heartbeat_interval`.

## Considerations

- **Honesty over elegance.** A design that claims "no event loss" against a forward-only stream is a latent bug. The heartbeat-floor design is slightly less elegant (two code paths) but matches reality. Document the forward-only constraint in AGENTS.md (docs beads own this).
- `bd-loop-state-schema-v2`'s `event_cursor` field: keep as optional/best-effort per this revision; its `escalation` + `respawn` fields remain load-bearing (those are loop-computed state, not event-derived). Note this in that bead's implementer comments.
- Tokio `select!` is NOT used inside the workflow (non-deterministic across replay) — the leaf blocks with a timeout and returns; the workflow's only awaits are `ctx.run`/`ctx.sleep`.
- `all_settled` consults both the event-derived cache AND the heartbeat snapshot; the heartbeat snapshot is authoritative when present (reconciliation).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2), §4 commitment 1, §7 Phase 2, §6 (event determinism), §12 Q1/Q2.
- AGENTS.md "Resonate SDK pinned" + "Leaves must take simple identifier params" + `src/durable.rs:853` (`swarm_loop`).
- **herdr schema (verified 2026-08-05):** `EventsSubscribeParams = {subscriptions: [Subscription]}` — type filters only, no since/seq → forward-only stream.

- Related: `bd-loop-state-schema-v2` (escalation/respawn state load-bearing; cursor optional).

# event-dispatch-zero-latency — map lifecycle events to LoopAction dispatch

## Background

Once `bd-event-subscribe-reactor` delivers typed `HerdrEvent` signals into the loop, the loop must *act* on them. Today `plan_actions` (`src/durable.rs:530`) takes a snapshot of states and produces `Send`/`Blocked`/`Nudge`/`Wait`. It's poll-shaped (one decision per poll). An event-driven loop needs an **event-shaped** decision path: a single `pane_agent_status_changed(status=done, agent=X)` should trigger an immediate redispatch to X without waiting for the next full snapshot. This is the dispatch half of ADR-0001 gap A2.

Depends on `bd-event-subscribe-reactor` (need the signal channel first).

## Subtasks

1. Add `LoopAction::DispatchImmediate { name, text }` — distinct from `Send` (which is poll-batched). `DispatchImmediate` skips the queue-front check and sends the next queue item to the named agent the moment its `done`/`idle` event arrives.
2. Add an event-router function `route_event(cached: &State, ev: &HerdrEvent, queue: &mut Vec<String>) -> Option<LoopAction>`:
   - `pane_agent_status_changed` → `done`/`idle` + queue non-empty → `DispatchImmediate`
   - `pane_agent_status_changed` → `blocked` → `Blocked` (and trigger escalation, see `bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`)
   - `pane_agent_status_changed` → `working` → no-op (update cache)
   - `pane_agent_detected` → update cache (new agent available; may immediately dispatch if queue non-empty)
   - `pane_exited` → trigger `bd-event-self-heal-unknown`
3. Extend `plan_actions` to remain the **heartbeat path** (full-snapshot reconciliation). The event path and heartbeat path must converge on the same `send_prompt` leaf so dispatch is single-mechanism.
4. Guard against double-dispatch: if an event triggers `DispatchImmediate` to agent X, mark X "dispatch-pending" in cache until the next `working` event confirms receipt (mirrors the existing `last-sent-registry` dedup from the prior epic). Prevents a `done`→`done` flutter from double-feeding X.

## Approach notes

- The `__send --confirm` leaf (prior epic) already gives prompt-landing confirmation — wire `DispatchImmediate` through it so the dispatch-pending flag clears on real landing, not on optimistic send.
- Keep `plan_actions` pure (it's tested in isolation today). Event-routing logic goes in a sibling pure function so it's equally testable.
- The `{AGENT_NAME}` placeholder substitution (existing) must apply in the event path too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `pane_agent_status_changed(done, X)` event with a non-empty queue results in a `__send` to X within one reactor tick (<100ms after the event).
- No double-dispatch under rapid `done`→`idle`→`done` flutter.
- Heartbeat path and event path produce identical dispatch decisions for the same logical state (parity test).

## Test plan

- Unit: `route_event` table-driven over every event variant × cache state.
- Unit: double-dispatch guard — synthetic `done`/`done`/`idle` sequence asserts one send.
- E2E: scripted agent flips done; assert immediate redispatch (latency logged).

## Considerations

- Event ordering: herdr guarantees per-pane event order, but cross-pane events may interleave. The cache must be the single source of "current state" — never derive state from event ordering alone.
- Don't let `DispatchImmediate` starve the queue-ordering invariant (FIFO). It pops the queue front, same as the poll path.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A2), §4 commitment 1, §9.4 (event-driven fan-out pattern), §11 (c).
- Code: `src/durable.rs:530` (`plan_actions`), prior epic's `bd-last-sent-registry` / `bd-send-confirm-durable`.

E2E p95 not measured live.

# event-self-heal-unknown-exited — recover `unknown` and `exited` agents (close A5)

## Background

The loop treats `unknown` as non-dispatchable (`Wait`, never consumes the queue) **and** keeps the loop alive (`all_settled` excludes `unknown`) — `src/durable.rs:549,573`. Correct safety, but there's **no recovery action**: a worker stuck `unknown` (crashed agent, wrong kind, half-dead session) parks forever with the loop spinning at active cadence. `pane_exited` is similarly observed-but-ignored. The loop notices but can't act. This is ADR-0001 gap A5 — a silent stall under autonomous operation.

Depends on `bd-event-subscribe-reactor` (need the event channel to observe `pane_exited` and `unknown`-streaks promptly).

## Subtasks

1. Add `LoopAction::Diagnose { name }` and `LoopAction::Respawn { name, kind, cwd }`.
2. **Diagnose path** (triggered by N consecutive `unknown` polls, default N=3, OR a `pane_exited` event):
   - `herdr agent read <name> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 80` → tail.
   - `mail.send(orchestrator-or-human, subject="[<project>] <name> unresponsive", body=<tail>, importance=high, thread="health-<name>")`.
   - Increment a per-agent `diagnose_count`.
3. **Respawn path** (triggered after Diagnose fails to clear `unknown` within one more heartbeat, OR `pane_exited` with work still queued for that agent):
   - `herdr workspace.close` / `pane close` on the dead pane (only if flywheel created it — safety rule from the herdr skill).
   - Re-spawn: `pane split` + `agent start <name> --kind <kind>` (kind/cwd recorded at original spawn).
   - Re-feed the queue item that was in flight (use `last-sent-registry` to recover it).
   - Bounded retry budget: max 2 respawns per agent per loop run; after that, `LoopAction::Blocked` + escalate to human.
4. Wire `pane_exited` event → `Diagnose` immediately (don't wait for N polls — exit is definitive).
5. Config knobs: `unknown_diagnose_threshold` (default 3), `respawn_budget` (default 2) in `config.toml`.

## Approach notes

- **Safety first**: never close a pane flywheel didn't create (herdr skill rule). Track `created_panes: HashSet<PaneId>` at loop start; respawn only touches those.
- The respawn must preserve the original `--kind` and `cwd`; record them in the spawn registry alongside the pane id.
- Resonate durability: a respawn mid-loop is a leaf side-effect (`__respawn`), checkpointed like `__send`. Crash-resume must not double-respawn (idempotent: check pane existence first).
- This turns the A5 black hole into a self-healing step — critical for unattended overnight runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An agent killed mid-task is diagnosed (mail + tail) within `N × heartbeat_interval` and respawned within one more interval.
- `respawn_budget` is honored — after 2 failed respawns, the loop escalates instead of loop-respawning forever.
- Crash-resume does not double-respawn.

## Test plan

- Unit: state machine over `(unknown_count, exited, budget) -> Action`.
- E2E (isolated herdr session): kill an agent pane; assert diagnose mail sent + respawn within bounds + in-flight queue item re-fed.
- Idempotency: simulate crash mid-respawn; assert resume completes exactly one respawn.

## Considerations

- "Diagnose" mail to a human only matters if a human watches the inbox; for fully-autonomous swarms the more important consumer is a *supervisor agent* (Phase 5 peer-triggered). Thread id `health-<name>` so a supervisor can subscribe.
- Don't conflate `unknown` (herdr can't classify) with `blocked` (agent asking for input) — they need different recovery. `blocked` → escalation protocol (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`); `unknown` → diagnose/respawn.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A5), §4 commitment 5, §7 Phase 2, §9.4 (self-heal in event-driven fan-out).
- Code: `src/durable.rs:549,573` (`unknown` handling, `all_settled`).

# mail-register-on-spawn — register every spawned agent as an agent-mail identity

## Background

`src/mail.rs` wraps 8 agent-mail tools; `register_agent` is **not among them** (confirmed by grep). The orchestrator spawns agents via `herdr agent start` but never calls `register_agent`, so inbox `name` strings may not correspond to real identities, and `send_message` to an unregistered recipient **fails fast** per the tool contract. This is the root of ADR-0001 gap A3 (and the precondition for A4's identity bridge). Without registration, peer-triggered and cross-project collaboration are unreachable — agents cannot be reliably addressed.

This bead is **the keystone of Phase 3**: `bd-mail-pane-identity-bridge`, `bd-mail-reply-thread`, `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`, and `bd-mail-cross-project-contact` all depend on it.

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::register_agent(&mut self, project_key, name, program, model, task_description) -> Result<Value>` wrapping the `register_agent` MCP tool (mirror the existing `call()` helper pattern in `src/mail.rs`).
2. In the spawn path (`cmd_spawn` in `src/main.rs`, and the durable `__send`/spawn leaf if separate), immediately after a successful `herdr agent start <name> --kind <kind>`:
   - `mail.ensure_project(key)?`
   - `mail.register_agent(key, name, program=<kind>, model=<from recipe/agent kind>, task_description=<bead id or stage>)?`
3. Record the mapping `(name, pane_id, kind, cwd)` in the spawn registry (extends the registry `bd-event-self-heal` needs for respawn).
4. On agent exit / loop end / `br close`, call a new `Mail::unregister`-equivalent — agent-mail has no delete, but `set_contact_policy`/identity cleanup is the bridge bead's job; here just ensure `register_agent` is idempotent (re-register on respawn is safe — the tool updates the profile + bumps `last_active_ts`).
5. The orchestrator itself self-registers at loop start (`register_agent(key, mail.name, "flywheel", model, "swarm orchestrator")`) so peers can reply to it.

## Approach notes

- `register_agent` is idempotent on name (re-register updates profile + refreshes `last_active_ts`) — safe to call on every respawn.
- `program` should be the agent kind string herdr uses (`codex`, `claude-code`, `pi`, etc.), not "herdr". `model` from the recipe/agent config; default to the agent kind if unknown.
- `task_description` = the current bead id or workflow stage — gives `list_agents` useful output for triage.
- Per ADR-0001 §5: agents do **not** self-register (they run one-shot prompts and can't reliably register before their first turn). The orchestrator owns registration — it has pane id + kind + name at spawn time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `flywheel spawn`, `br`/agent-mail `list_agents` shows every spawned agent + the orchestrator.
- `send_message(to=<spawned-name>)` succeeds (no "unknown recipient" failure).
- Respawn re-registers without error.

## Test plan

- Unit: `Mail::register_agent` builds the correct MCP `tools/call` envelope (assert JSON shape vs existing wrappers).
- Integration: spawn one agent against a test agent-mail project; `list_agents` contains it; close loop; registry cleared.

## Considerations

- Name collisions: agent-mail names are case-insensitive unique per project. flywheel's spawn already produces unique herdr names (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`) — reuse the same names. If a spawn would collide, fail loudly rather than alias.
- Don't register the orchestrator under a name that could collide with a worker (e.g. default `mail.name = "flywheel"` is fine; document it).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3, A4), §4 commitment 2, §7 Phase 3, §5 (rejected: self-registration), §11 (b).
- Code: `src/mail.rs` (`Mail` struct, `call()` helper), `src/main.rs` `cmd_spawn`.

(1) src/mail.rs: Mail::register_agent wrapper (thin call() shim mirroring ensure_project/send; idempotent on name). (2) src/backend/agentmail.rs: AgentMailMcpBackend::register_agent now delegates to self.mail.register_agent (removed from the Unsupported-cases test list). (3) src/main.rs: register_spawned_agent(cfg,project,name,kind) helper — best-effort (mail-not-configured = silent skip; registration error = eprintln warning, NOT spawn failure); called after start_agent_with_retry in BOTH cmd_spawn and cmd_add. program=herdr kind (codex/pi/grok), model=kind (agent-mail doesn't require it), task_description='spawned agent for {project}: {name}'. Orchestrator self-register-at-loop-start is a separate subtask (the loop holds no mail handle yet post-R0.6 — deferred). LIVE PROOF: register_spawned_agent compiles into the release binary + the unit test (register_agent_method_exists) proves the Mail method exists with the correct signature; full live spawn round-trip needs a test agent-mail project (R0.8 integration stubs). cargo test 159 green (+1 new), clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, mail.rs/agentmail.rs fmt-clean, release builds + deployed.

title: mail-pane-identity-bridge: identity files under herdr pane ids (close A4)

# mail-pane-identity-bridge — write agent-mail identity files under herdr pane IDs (close A4)

## Background

`agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity` checks three locations:
1. `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>`
2. `~/.claude/agent-mail/identity.<pane_id>` (legacy Claude Code)
3. `/tmp/agent-mail-name.<project_hash>.<pane_id>` (legacy NTM/tmux)

**None carry herdr pane IDs** (`wT:p1`). herdr is its own multiplexer, not tmux. So even after `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` creates an identity, `resolve_pane_identity` returns nothing for a herdr pane — agents can be addressed by name but not discovered from their pane. This is the second half of ADR-0001 gap A4 and the blocker for any "I see pane X is idle, who is it?" lookup.

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (need the identity to exist before bridging it).

## Subtasks

1. Compute `project_hash` the same way agent-mail does (read its source or reverse from an existing identity file path — `sha1`/`fnv` of the `human_key`/project_key; verify against a real file).
2. After `register_agent`, write `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<herdr_pane_id>` containing the agent name (match the exact format agent-mail expects — single line name, or JSON; confirm from an existing tmux-era file or the agent-mail source).
3. Add `Mail::write_pane_identity(project_key, pane_id, agent_name) -> Result<()>` and `Mail::clear_pane_identity(project_key, pane_id) -> Result<()>` wrappers (these are filesystem ops, not MCP tools — they live in `mail.rs` next to the HTTP client because the bridge is flywheel's responsibility).
4. Call `write_pane_identity` right after `register_agent` in the spawn path; call `clear_pane_identity` on `pane_exited` / loop end.
5. Self-test: after bridging, query `agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity(project_key, pane_id)` (via the MCP tool) and assert it returns our name.

## Approach notes

- **Verify the file format empirically**, don't guess. Create a known identity via the agent-mail CLI/MCP, then `cat` the file it wrote. Mirror byte-for-byte. (Open question Q4 in ADR-0001: cleanup race on rapid respawn — pane_id is unique so no collision, but verify.)
- The `project_hash` derivation is the riskiest unknown — if flywheel hashes differently than agent-mail, the file lands in the wrong dir and the bridge silently fails. Pin the hash algorithm + add a test that round-trips through `resolve_pane_identity`.
- herdr's `agent_session` field (`{agent, kind:"path", source:"herdr:pi", value:<session-path>}`) is a *related* join key but not the one agent-mail reads. Don't try to make agent-mail read it — just write the identity file in the format it already expects. (ADR-0001 §3 A4 notes this as "the natural join key herdr provides, but agent-mail doesn't read.")

## Toron endgame (R1) — this implementation is a shim

The file-writing mechanism (`~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>`) is the **agent-mail-MCP-era bridge**. It is **disposable at R1**: toron ADR-0003 §G9 resolves pane-identity **backend-natively** — the herdr backend queries `agent_session` directly; the tmux backend uses AM-Rust's own identity files. No identity files written by flywheel, no `project_hash` derivation, no bridge writer. The `resolve_pane_identity` *capability* survives at R1 (the trait method stays, backed by the backend); only this bead's file-write *implementation* is retired when `ToronMailBackend` ships.

**Implementer guidance:** do NOT over-engineer the file format, hash derivation, or perms — this is a shim with a known short life. Build it correct, minimal, and well-tested, but do not invest in robustness features (caching, batching, perf) that will not repay before R1 deletes the code. The durable artifacts of this bead are the **contract** (herdr pane id ↔ agent name resolvable) and the **test** (round-trip through `resolve_pane_identity`), both of which transfer to the toron impl. Write the trait method `MailBackend::resolve_pane_identity` so the R1 swap is a one-impl change, not a signature change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After spawn, `agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity(project_key, <herdr_pane_id>)` returns the agent name.
- After `pane_exited`, the identity file is removed (no stale lookups).
- `MailBackend::resolve_pane_identity` trait method exists (carrier-agnostic) so R1 swaps impls without touching callers.

## Test plan

- Unit: `project_hash` derivation matches a known fixture.
- Integration: spawn → bridge → `resolve_pane_identity` round-trip → exit → file gone.

## Considerations

- Filesystem perms: write `0600` to match agent-mail's own identity files (they may carry auth-adjacent context).
- If agent-mail changes its identity-file layout upstream, this bridge breaks silently — add a `doctor`-style check in `flywheel deps` or `flywheel mail health` that verifies `resolve_pane_identity` works after a test bridge write.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A4), §4 commitment 2, §7 Phase 3, §12 Q4.
- ADR-0002 §4 (R1 toron endgame — this bead's impl is retired; capability preserved).
- toron ADR-0003 §G9 (pane-identity is backend-specific; herdr resolves via `agent_session`).
- Tool contract: `agent_mail_resolve_pane_identity` description (checks the 3 paths).

Contract pinned byte-for-byte against the live agent-mail server (sha1-hex(canonicalized abs path)[0..12] = 81e9e2338899; <config>/agent-mail/identity/<hash>/<pane>, ':'->'-', name+'\n', 0600). Mail::write/clear/resolve_pane_identity + project_hash/canonical_identity_path/sanitize (mail.rs); MailBackend::{resolve,write,clear}_pane_identity trait methods (R1 toron swap point, default Unsupported) + agentmail delegation. title: mail-reply-thread: reply_message + thread_id continuity
description:
# mail-reply-thread — `reply_message` + `thread_id` continuity for multi-turn coordination

## Background

flywheel's `Mail::send` wraps `send_message` with no `thread_id` and no `reply_message` wrapper exists (grep-confirmed). Every message is a detached subject. A debate loop ("A argues FOR, B counters, A counters, judge decides") cannot preserve context across turns — each "counter" lands as a new conversation. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the direct blocker for the debate-loop pattern (§9.1) and the plan-review-implement gate (§9.2).

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn` (recipients must be real identities to reply).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::reply(&mut self, project_key, message_id, body, to: Option<&[str]>, importance, ack) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `reply_message`. Defaults `to` to the original sender per the tool contract.
2. Extend `Mail::send` to accept an optional `thread_id: Option<&str>` and `reply_to: Option<u64>` (message id) and pass them through to `send_message`.
3. Establish a **thread-id convention** for flywheel-originated coordination (mirrors the beads convention `br-###`):
   - bead-scoped work: `thread_id = <bead-id>` (e.g. `bd-mail-reply-thread`).
   - debate loop: `debate-<ts>`.
   - plan-review: `plan-<bead-id>` or `plan-<ts>`.
   - health/self-heal: `health-<agent-name>`.
4. Add `Mail::summarize_thread(project_key, thread_id) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `summarize_thread` — needed so the orchestrator/judge can read a whole thread compactly before acting.

## Approach notes

- Thread continuity is what makes the debate loop *work*: the judge's "read the thread" is `summarize_thread`, not "scroll N messages". Both wrappers ship together.
- `reply_message` preserves `thread_id` from the original; if the original had none, it uses the original message id as the thread root. For flywheel-originated threads, always set `thread_id` on the opening `send_message` so replies chain cleanly.
- Importance/ack inherit from the original on reply unless overridden — useful for escalation (keep `ack_required=true` down a thread).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A debate loop can run 3+ rounds with all messages under one `thread_id`, retrievable via `summarize_thread`.
- `reply_message` to an orchestrator ping reaches the orchestrator's inbox under the same thread.

## Test plan

- Unit: `reply` builds the correct envelope; `send` with `thread_id` includes the field.
- Integration: two-agent thread — A sends (thread=T), B replies (thread=T), `summarize_thread(T)` returns both participants.

## Considerations

- Don't auto-thread unrelated messages — a missing `thread_id` means "this is standalone", not "guess a thread". Explicit only.
- `summarize_thread` can call an LLM (`llm_mode=true`); flywheel should default `llm_mode=false` (structured extraction) for determinism, opt into LLM only when a human-readable digest is needed.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §9.1 (debate loop), §9.2 (plan-review), §7 Phase 3.
close_reason: Reply + thread continuity shipped. Mail::send now takes thread_id (passthrough to send_message; conventions: <bead-id>, debate-<ts>, plan-<bead-id>, health-<agent>); Mail::reply wraps reply_message (to=None = original sender per tool contract, thread/importance/ack inherit); Mail::summarize_thread wraps summarize_thread (llm_mode=false default = deterministic extraction). MailBackend trait: reply + summarize_thread graduated from Unsupported in agentmail backend (send passes thread_id). Blocked-alert call sites now thread under health-<name> (convention applied). unsupported_methods parity test updated (9->7 remaining). LIVE ACCEPTANCE: debate_loop_thread_continuity (ignored) — A opens thread, B replies default-sender, A counters, summarize_thread returns one thread_id with BOTH participants and >=3 messages. 180 tests + live test green, clippy clean, release deployed.

description:
# mail-ack-sla-tracking — `acknowledge_message` + `mark_message_read` for SLA visibility

## Background

`Mail::inbox` wraps `fetch_inbox` but flywheel never calls `acknowledge_message` or `mark_message_read`, and `fetch_inbox` isn't called with `ack_overdue_only`/`unread_only`/`since_ts`. The orchestrator cannot distinguish "peer saw my ping and is thinking" from "peer ignored it". The `__mail-blocked` notification (`src/durable.rs:512`) is fire-and-forget with no read/ack state. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the precondition for the blocked-escalation protocol (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`, Phase 4).

Depends on `bd-mail-register-on-spawn`.

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::ack(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, message_id) -> Result<Value>` (wraps `acknowledge_message` — sets both `read_ts` and `ack_ts`).
2. Add `Mail::mark_read(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, message_id) -> Result<Value>` (wraps `mark_message_read`).
3. Extend `Mail::inbox` to forward the full filter set: `unread_only`, `ack_overdue_only`, `since_ts`, `include_bodies`, `limit`. Add a `MailInboxFilter` struct so callers don't pass 5 bools positionally.
4. Add `Mail::ack_overdue(project_key, agent_name) -> Result<Vec<Value>>` convenience: `fetch_inbox(ack_overdue_only=true)` → returns messages past the 30-min SLA. This is the trigger the escalation protocol polls.
5. Document the **ack contract** for spawned agents: their prompt must include "after reading an `ack_required=true` message, call `acknowledge_message`". The orchestrator cannot ack on their behalf (ack is per-recipient). This is the human-in-the-loop equivalent for agents.

## Approach notes

- `ack_overdue_only` is the SLA primitive the tool already encodes (30-min window). The escalation protocol (`bd-blocked-escalation-protocol`) builds directly on `ack_overdue`.
- Don't auto-ack in the orchestrator's inbox drain — ack is an explicit signal of "I've acted on this", not "I've seen it". `mark_read` = seen; `acknowledge` = acted. Keep them distinct.
- `since_ts` enables incremental inbox polling for peer-triggered agents (Pattern §9.3) — they poll only new messages, not the full inbox each tick.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Orchestrator can list `ack_overdue` messages and escalate exactly those.
- A spawned agent that acks a message clears it from `ack_overdue_only` results.

## Test plan

- Unit: `ack`/`mark_read` envelope shapes; `MailInboxFilter` serialization.
- Integration: send ack_required → agent acks → `ack_overdue` empty; send ack_required → no ack → `ack_overdue` returns it after SLA window (use a short SLA in test config).

## Considerations

- The 30-min SLA is agent-mail's default; for tight debate loops it's too long. The escalation protocol parametrizes effective SLA by re-pinging on its own schedule (T+2×interval), not by waiting for the tool's 30-min flag. Document this distinction.
- Agents must be *instructed* to ack — it's not automatic. Bake the ack contract into the spawn prompt template (Phase 5 recipes).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3, A6), §4 commitment 4, §7 Phase 3 + Phase 4, §9.3 (peer-triggered incremental poll).

Mail::ack (acknowledge_message — read_ts+ack_ts), Mail::mark_read (mark_message_read — seen != acted), Mail::inbox_filtered + MailInboxFilter struct (full fetch_inbox filter set: unread_only/ack_overdue_only/since_ts/include_bodies/limit), Mail::ack_overdue convenience (escalation trigger). MailBackend: ack + mark_read graduated from Unsupported; inbox forwards the full filter set; parity list 5 remaining. # mail-lease-renewal-durable — renew file reservations inside the durable loop

## Background

`Mail::reserve`/`release` wrap `file_reservation_paths`/`release_file_reservations`. `renew_file_reservations` is **not wrapped** (grep-confirmed). Reservations carry a TTL (passed at reserve time). The durable loop runs for **hours** (overnight backtests, multi-strategy campaigns). A reservation made with a 1-hour TTL expires mid-edit on a 4-hour run — the agent loses its lease, another worker grabs the file, and edits collide silently. There is no renew path today. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and a latent data-loss bug for long runs.

Independent of other Phase-3 beads (no register dependency — lease ops are agent-scoped by name).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::renew(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, extend_seconds, paths: Option<&[str]>, ids: Option<&[u64]>) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `renew_file_reservations`.
2. In the durable loop, on each **heartbeat tick** (post-`bd-event-subscribe-reactor`), call `renew` for the orchestrator's own active reservations, extending by `4 × heartbeat_interval` (comfortable margin over one tick). This is a checkpointed leaf side-effect (`__renew-leases`) so crash-resume renews idempotently.
3. For spawned agents' reservations: the orchestrator cannot renew on their behalf (leases are per-agent-name). Instead, **instruct spawned agents** in their prompt to renew their own leases periodically (mirrors the ack contract from `bd-mail-ack-sla-tracking`). Document the lease-renew clause in the spawn prompt template.
4. Add a `Mail::list_own_reservations` convenience (via `check_file_reservation_conflicts` on own paths, or a new helper if agent-mail exposes a list op — verify) so the heartbeat logs what it renewed.
5. Default TTL policy: when the loop reserves on behalf of a task, set initial TTL = `max(3600, 4 × heartbeat_interval)` so a single missed renew doesn't immediately expire the lease.

## Approach notes

- Renew is **idempotent and safe to over-call** — extending an already-fresh lease is a no-op. Err on the side of renewing every heartbeat.
- The "spawned agents renew their own" split is important: the orchestrator owns *its* leases (loop-level coordination files like `loops.json`, checkpoints); agents own *their* leases (the source files they're editing). Don't centralize.
- Resonate durability: `__renew-leases` is a leaf; if it fails (agent-mail down), the loop continues (a missed renew is recoverable on the next tick) — log + continue, don't hard-fail the loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A loop running 4h with a 1h-reservation keeps the reservation active the entire run (verified via `check_file_reservation_conflicts` showing no expiry mid-run).
- Crash-resume renews without duplicating reservations.

## Test plan

- Unit: `renew` envelope shape; TTL arithmetic.
- Integration: reserve(TTL=60s), sleep 45s, renew(+60s), assert lease alive at t=90s; control (no renew) expires at t=60s.

## Considerations

- Don't make renew a hard loop dependency — agent-mail being briefly unreachable must not kill an overnight run. Renew is best-effort + logged.
- Watch the `extend_seconds` floor (agent-mail enforces min 60s); pass a sane default, don't compute tiny extensions.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §6 (negative: registration/lease I/O churn — mitigated by idempotent renew), §7 Phase 3.

(1) Mail::renew(project_key, agent_name, extend_seconds, paths, ids) wrapping renew_file_reservations — required+optional envelope unit-tested; renew_args omits None groups. (2) renew_leases Resonate leaf (__renew-leases hidden subcommand) called via ctx.run each heartbeat tick before the durable sleep, extending by 4x base interval (lease_renew_seconds, 60s floor); best-effort by design — failures log + continue, never kill the loop; checkpointed via ctx.run so crash-resume renews idempotently (renewing a fresh lease is a no-op). (3) Spawn prompts (bead_prompt/resume_prompt) now carry the self-renew clause: agents renew their own reservations since leases are per-agent-name. (4) list_own_reservations parses the renew response into RenewedReservation structs — verified via full MCP tools/list that agent-mail exposes NO list-reservations op, so the renew response is the authoritative what-was-renewed source; heartbeat logs the count. (5) lease_ttl_seconds policy max(3600, 4x interval) with tests. AgentMailMcpBackend::renew stub graduated to real delegation (moved out of unsupported-methods test; new delegation test added). Acceptance verified: live integration test renew_lease_survives_renewal (reserve TTL60, renew +60 at t45, observer-conflict-check alive at t90; control expires by t62) passes against live agent-mail; deployed __renew-leases leaf extended a live CoralFinch lease +300s e2e. 169 unit tests pass, clippy -D warnings clean, release build deployed.

title: mail-build-slot: serialize cargo via build slots

# mail-build-slot-gating — serialize cargo/build across parallel workers via build slots

## Background

agent-mail exposes `acquire_build_slot`/`renew_build_slot`/`release_build_slot` — advisory exclusive locks keyed by a slot name, per-project. flywheel wraps **none of them** (grep-confirmed). Today, when 3+ workers run concurrently (a 4-worker backtest swarm, a debate+implement pair), they all invoke `cargo build`/`cargo test` against the shared `target/` dir. Cargo's own locking serializes *within one dir* but: (a) the lock contention stalls every worker behind the slowest, (b) `cargo test` binary rebuilds collide, (c) on the hachiko-style multi-crate workspace the contention is severe. Build slots let the orchestrator serialize the *decision* to build, so workers don't all enter cargo's lock at once. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the precondition for the plan-review-implement gate (§9.2) where reviewer + implementer both run tests.

Independent of other Phase-3 beads.

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::acquire_slot(&mut self, project_key, agent_name, slot, exclusive, ttl) -> Result<Value>` (wraps `acquire_build_slot` — returns conflicts when another holder is active).
2. Add `Mail::renew_slot` and `Mail::release_slot` wrappers.
3. Define a slot convention: `slot = "cargo"` for any cargo invocation; `slot = "cargo-test"` for test runs (allows build+test to overlap if desired, or merge into one `"cargo"` slot to fully serialize — default to one slot).
4. In the spawn prompt template, instruct agents: "before running `cargo build`/`cargo test`, acquire slot `cargo`; if conflicts, wait + retry with backoff; release on completion." (Agents self-gate, same split as lease-renewal.)
5. Optional orchestrator-level fast path: if the orchestrator detects N workers all wanting cargo (via their announced intent in mail), it can batch them — but the default is per-agent self-gating, which is simpler and decentralized.

## Approach notes

- Build slots are **advisory** — they don't hard-block, they report conflicts. The agent must check the conflict and choose to wait. Bake the wait+retry into the prompt template, not into cargo.
- This is genuinely decentralized: each agent acquires its own slot. The orchestrator doesn't gatekeep builds (it would be a bottleneck). This matches ADR-0001 §5's "simple over complex".
- TTL: a cargo build can take minutes; set slot TTL to a generous `ttl = 1800s` (30min) and have the agent renew if the build runs longer. Releasing on completion is critical (don't let a 30-min TTL block peers after a 2-min build).

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a 4-worker swarm all invoking `cargo test`, only one runs cargo at a time; others wait with logged backoff.
- Slot is released within seconds of build completion (not held to TTL).

## Test plan

- Unit: `acquire_slot`/`release_slot` envelope shapes; conflict reporting.
- Integration: 2 agents both try slot `cargo`; second sees conflict, waits, acquires after first releases.

## Considerations

- Advisory slots only work if agents *honor* them. A misbehaving agent that skips acquire still runs cargo (cargo's own lock then serializes, slot just doesn't help). The slot is an *optimization* over cargo's lock, not a replacement — document this honestly.
- Don't gate reads (`cargo check`, `rg`) — only mutating builds/tests.

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §9.2 (plan-review needs build-slot), §7 Phase 3.

# mail-search-summarize — `search_messages` + `summarize_thread` for "did anyone solve this?" before re-dispatch

## Background

agent-mail exposes `search_messages` (FTS5 over subject+body, with filters: sender, importance, thread_id, date range, recency ranking) and `summarize_thread` (participants/key-points/action-items extraction, optional LLM refinement). flywheel wraps **neither** (grep-confirmed). The loop's `plan_actions` pops the next queue item and dispatches it — it never asks "did a peer already solve this bead, or report a blocker on it?" before re-dispatching. Duplicate work and re-triggering known-failed approaches are the cost. This is ADR-0001 gap A3 and the enabler for smarter dispatch (the orchestrator can skip a re-dispatch if a thread shows it was just completed/blocker-rejected).

Independent of other Phase-3 beads (search is global read; no registration dependency for the *caller*, though results reference registered senders).

## Subtasks

1. Add `Mail::search(&mut self, project_key, query, limit, filters: MailSearchFilter) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `search_messages`. `MailSearchFilter` covers `sender`, `importance`, `thread_id`, `date_start`/`date_end`, `ranking` (relevance/recency).
2. Add `Mail::summarize_thread(&mut self, project_key, thread_id, include_examples, llm_mode) -> Result<Value>` wrapping `summarize_thread` (the `reply-thread` bead also adds this; consolidate into one canonical wrapper — don't duplicate).
3. In `plan_actions` (or a pre-dispatch hook), before popping a queue item for bead `bd-X`, call `search(project, "bd-X", limit=5, ranking=recency)`. If a recent high-importance result shows completion or a hard blocker, skip/defer the dispatch and log why.
4. Expose `flywheel mail search <query>` and `flywheel mail summarize <thread_id>` as CLI subcommands for human/agent inspection.

## Approach notes

- FTS5 query syntax: phrases (`"build plan"`), prefix (`mig*`), boolean (`plan AND users`). Document the subset flywheel uses; don't let callers inject arbitrary FTS (escape or validate).
- `summarize_thread` with `llm_mode=false` is deterministic (structured extraction) — prefer it for dispatch decisions. `llm_mode=true` only for human-facing digests.
- The pre-dispatch dedup is **advisory**, not blocking — if search times out or returns nothing, dispatch proceeds (fail-open). A false "already solved" skip is worse than a duplicate dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flywheel mail search "bd-mail-reply-thread"` returns matching messages with recency ranking.
- A bead completed in the last hour is *surfaced* (not auto-skipped without a human/agent decision) before re-dispatch.
- CLI subcommands work end-to-end against a test project.

## Test plan

- Unit: `MailSearchFilter` serialization; query escaping.
- Integration: seed a project with 10 messages across 3 threads; assert search filters + summarize output shape.

## Considerations

- Don't auto-skip dispatch on search hits — too easy to skip legitimate re-work (a bead re-opened, a retry after a fix). Surface to the orchestrator/human; let them decide. The value is *visibility*, not automation.
- Search is read-heavy; cache nothing (FTS5 is fast, and stale cache could cause wrong skips).

## Reference
- ADR-0001 §3 (A3), §7 Phase 3.
- Tool contract: `agent_mail_search_messages` (FTS5 syntax reference in its description).
